title: Design: Credit Terms page and table look as designed
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • Scenario: Your shop has every standard term switched on, and you compare the Credit Terms page with the design.
  • You are an Admin user working at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • All twelve standard terms are active and COD is the default for new customers.
  • The browser window is 1440 px wide, at 100% zoom.
    For example: a maximised window on a 1440 x 900 screen.
  • The design pictures ct-p1-01-active-tab-one-table.png, ct-p1-05-row-menu-a-standard-term.png are attached to this case; open each at 100% zoom beside the screen.
  • Starting screen: the Settings page.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. In the Settings menu, click "Credit Terms".
  2. Resize the browser window to 1536 px wide (for example, maximise it on a 1536 x 864 screen at 100% zoom).
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the page matches the attached picture ct-p1-01-active-tab-one-table.png: in the side menu the Finance group shows "Payment Methods" and, directly below it, "Credit Terms" with a clock icon, in blue because it is open. The title "Credit Terms" is at the top left; at the top right are a square outlined "⋯" button and, right of it, the only blue button on the page, "+ New Credit Term". Below are the "Active" and "Inactive" tabs, then one table (no sections, no card around it) with the headings Name, Due, Customers and Vendors and a last column with no heading. Customers and Vendors counts are right aligned and 0 shows as 0. Every row is one line and ends with a grey "⋯". Only COD, Due on Receipt and Credit Hold show an info (i) icon and a lock icon after the name. The heading style and the font: this attribute depends on question 12 (drawn pictures or build pictures, not answered yet): for now compare it with the picture named here (ct-p1-01-active-tab-one-table.png draws small grey headings, the build picture ct-p1-05-row-menu-a-standard-term.png bold black ones).
  • Step 2: at 1536 px nothing overlaps, nothing is cut off and nothing needs a sideways scroll; the layout described above is unchanged, only wider.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11670 (Story 1, Credit Terms page and list)

  • S1-R1: “Under Settings, in the Finance group, a "Credit Terms" item appears directly below "Payment Methods". Selecting it opens the Credit Terms page.”
  • S1-R2: “The page header shows the title "Credit Terms" and, top right, a primary "New Credit Term" button (Story 3: Create or edit a credit term) with a "⋯" page menu beside it (Story 12: Credit Terms audit log).”
  • S1-R3: “Below the header are two tabs, "Active" and "Inactive", each followed by a count of the terms in it. The page opens on Active.”
  • S1-R4: “Each tab shows one table with the columns Name, Due, Customers, Vendors, and an unlabeled actions column holding the row's "⋯" menu (Story 2: Row menu actions). The columns keep the same widths on both tabs.”
  • S1-R10: “No other term (standard Net terms and every term the shop created) shows an info icon or a lock icon.”
  • S1-R12: “The Customers column shows how many customers hold the term, right aligned, showing 0 when none. The Counter Sale customer is never counted. A customer with a blank term is counted under COD. Names that differ only in capitals and spaces count toward the same term ("NET 30" counts as Net 30; see §6).”
  • S1-R13: “The Vendors column shows how many vendors hold the term, right aligned, 0 when none, by the same rules as S1-R12 (a blank vendor term counts under COD).”
  • S1-N3: “Every row has a "⋯" menu, because "Move Customers" appears on every row for every user who can open the page (S2-R1), greyed when it cannot be used. Credit Hold and the default COD row therefore always have a menu.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "Default Credit Terms" (https://claude.ai/artifact/2erYxWz2ffDNcoXzEfu6wf), read 23 Oct 2026: page "1 List and row menus" ("Active tab: one table", "Row menu: a standard term"). Compare the screen with the pictures below; the expected results above come from the PRD quotes, except where this held design case follows the design.

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • ct-p1-01-active-tab-one-table.png
  • ct-p1-05-row-menu-a-standard-term.png

The design's own words:

  • “One table per tab, no sections. Columns: Name, Due, Customers, Vendors, ⋯.”
  • “The default row carries a "Default" badge. New Credit Term is the one primary button, top right; the page ⋯ menu (Audit Log) sits beside it.”
  • “Source: Payment Methods puts its one add button, "New payment method", at the top right. DS rule: one primary button per view.”
